findings.issue: A-3 says the message clears when the user makes the next change, not when that change saves. The test only asserts the alert is gone after a save that succeeds within milliseconds, so moving setSettingsSaveFailed(false) from changeSettings into the 'saved' branch would still pass. SPEC-02's literal Then is met, so this is not blocking.
findings.evidence: setPutsFail(false); keyboard Space; expect(alert).toHaveCount(0). The same result happens whether the flag clears on change or on success.
findings.fix: Optionally use a held write (e2e/support/hold-writes.ts pattern) so the alert can be checked as gone while the second save is still pending. Or accept the gap, since the spec's SPEC-02 wording is met.

findings.issue: useRef(createSettingsSaver(...)) runs createSettingsSaver on every App render and throws the result away after the first one. It is harmless, but wasteful.
findings.evidence: The useRef argument is evaluated on every render. The spec's Design section prescribes this exact form.
findings.fix: Optional: const [saver] = useState(() => createSettingsSaver(...)) and drop .current. Or leave it as the spec wrote it.

findings.issue: A new backlog task about a CI timeout, unrelated to TASK-12.11, was committed on this branch. It is probably the orchestrator's follow-up-task process and not builder scope creep.
findings.fix: No code change. Confirm it belongs on this branch.

summary: All five SPEC items are implemented as specified and pass a mutation-style read of the code. The saver's sequence guard, the saved-on-success update, setSaved, and revertTo read at settle time are each caught by a unit test. Markup position and absence are both asserted. The e2e covers the revert, focus, the unchanged raw record, the log, axe, clearing on the next change, and clearing on reopen. The recorded deviation (an optional error on 'superseded' so App can log an older failed write) correctly carries out A-6 and is tested. writeSettings is async, so a synchronous put throw becomes a rejection. The two new vitest files pass, and the new Playwright spec passes on Chromium and WebKit. There are no BLOCKER or MAJOR findings: one MINOR (the clear-on-change timing is not distinguished from clear-on-success) and two NITs.
